title: Products in the derived category are termwise
statement:
Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and let $(K_i)_{i\in I}$ be a
family of complexes of $\mathcal R$-modules. Then the termwise product complex
$\prod_iK_i$ is a product of the $K_i$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)$, and
$H^p(\prod_iK_i)\cong\prod_iH^p(K_i)$ for every $p$. If $K_i\to K'_i$ are
quasi-isomorphisms, so is $\prod_iK_i\to\prod_iK'_i$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)$. Its set-indexed products exist as in [det-pe-products-exact]. Form $P^n=\prod_iK_i^n$ and define $d_P^n$ by $\pi_i^{n+1}d_P^n=d_i^n\pi_i^n$. The identities $d_P^{n+1}d_P^n=0$ follow after composing with each projection. Likewise the projections are chain maps, and any family of chain maps to the $K_i$ assembles uniquely degree by degree to a chain map to $P$. Thus $P$ is the termwise product complex, with its specified projections [def-weil-category-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Cohomology paragraph: the termwise product complex

proof.text: Fix $p$ and write $Z_i^p=\ker d_i^p$, $B_i^p=\operatorname{im}d_i^{p-1}$ and $H_i^p=Z_i^p/B_i^p$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Applying [det-pe-products-exact] to $0\to Z_i^p\to K_i^p\to B_i^{p+1}\to0$ identifies $\ker d_P^p$ with $\prod_i Z_i^p$: the factorization of $d_P^p$ through $\prod_i B_i^{p+1}\hookrightarrow\prod_iK_i^{p+1}$ has first map epimorphic and second map monomorphic. At degree $p-1$ the same factorization identifies $\operatorname{im}d_P^{p-1}$ with $\prod_iB_i^p$. Applying exactness again to $0\to B_i^p\to Z_i^p\to H_i^p\to0$ identifies the quotient with $\prod_iH_i^p$. Hence the morphism induced by the projections is $H^p(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i H^p(K_i)$. All these identifications commute with morphisms of families: their maps are characterized by the same projections, kernel inclusions and quotient maps. This proves the cohomology clause naturally in $(K_i)$.

source.place: Cohomology paragraph: kernels, images and cokernels

proof.text: For a family of quasi-isomorphisms $f_i:K_i\to K'_i$, naturality in the preceding step identifies $H^p(\prod_i f_i)$ with $\prod_i H^p(f_i)$. The latter is an isomorphism: the product of the inverses of $H^p(f_i)$ is its inverse, as checked after each projection [def-weil-category-product]. Therefore $\prod_i f_i$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every such family, by the definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Use the small representative of the site and universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. The theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] applies to this site and the arbitrary sheaf of rings $\mathcal R$, so $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck abelian; no commutativity or constant-coefficient assumption is required. By [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective], choose quasi-isomorphisms $r_i:K_i\to J_i$ with $J_i$ K-injective. The degreewise products of the $J_i$ exist by [det-pe-products-exact]. Apply [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective] in this abelian category to obtain that $J=\prod_i J_i$, with the degreewise projections $q_i$, is K-injective and that its image is a product of the $QJ_i$ in $D(\mathcal A)$. Here $Q$ is the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $r=\prod_i r_i:P\to J$ and let $\pi_i:P\to K_i$ be the projections. Step 3 says $r$ is a quasi-isomorphism, hence $Qr$ and all $Qr_i$ are isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The chain-map identities are $q_i r=r_i\pi_i$. For any object $C$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ and arrows $f_i:C\to QK_i$, use the product obtained in Step 4 to get the unique $g:C\to QJ$ with $Qq_i\,g=Qr_i\,f_i$. Put $h=(Qr)^{-1}g$. Then $Qr_i\,Q\pi_i\,h=Qq_i\,Qr\,h=Qr_i\,f_i$, so $Q\pi_i\,h=f_i$. If $h'$ has the same components, the product property of $QJ$ gives $Qr\,h'=g$ and hence $h'=h$. Thus the images of the actual termwise projections make $QP$ a product of the $QK_i$ [def-weil-category-product], proving the remaining clause, including uniqueness for arbitrary derived-category morphisms.

lean.statement: theorem products_derived (X : Scheme.{t}) (R : Sheaf (topology X) RingCat.{max u (t + 1)}) (I : Type u) [HasDerivedCategory.{v} (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R)] (K : I → CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) ℤ) : Nonempty (IsLimit (DerivedCategory.Q.mapCone (limit.cone (Discrete.functor K)))) ∧ (∀ p : ℤ, IsIso (piComparison (HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) p) K)) ∧ (∀ (K' : I → CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) ℤ) (f : ∀ i : I, K i ⟶ K' i), (∀ i : I, QuasiIso (f i)) → QuasiIso (Limits.Pi.map f))
